title: The Solar System
seo_title: Year 5 Science: The Solar System Worksheets (Planets, Orbits and Distances)
standard_text: Describe the movement of the Earth, and other planets, relative to the Sun in the solar system. Describe the Sun, Earth and Moon as approximately spherical bodies.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on the solar system: the Sun and the eight planets in order, planet facts, orbit times, distances from the Sun and how ideas about space changed. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The further a planet is from the Sun, the longer its year.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system; eight planets orbit it.

  • In order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (rocky), Jupiter, Saturn (gas giants), Uranus, Neptune (ice giants).
  • Planets further from the Sun take longer to orbit: Earth takes 365 days, Neptune 165 years.
  • The Sun, Earth and Moon are roughly spheres. The Moon orbits the Earth.
Example

Which planet is 4th from the Sun?

Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars

Answer: Mars

Example

Mars 687 days, Earth 365 days. Difference?

687 − 365

Answer: 322 days

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves round the Earth.
  • Calling Pluto or the Moon a planet.
  • Thinking planets further out orbit faster.

faq.q: What are the planets in order?
faq.a: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. A rhyme such as 'My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Naming' helps.

faq.q: Why do outer planets have longer years?
faq.a: They are further from the Sun, so they have a much longer path to travel and move more slowly in their orbit.
Not any more. Since 2006 Pluto has been classed as a dwarf planet.
